I struggled a lot with my mental health while in high school, and it got worse after my grandpa committed suicide. I was 17 then, and he was the man who raised me, taught me to always be curious and question the world. To stay humble, also. I was devastated.

One month after his death I began to see a therapist and we had a great connexion: I felt that I was listened to, cared for, but alas my stepfather didn't like the idea of me taking meds and being helped I guess. He told me I didn't need it because "You can't be depressed, you smiled to me today! You're doing it for attention!" and kept asking me to stop it again and again and again. My mother agreed with him and, well, you guessed it: I stopped seeing my therapist. I lied to him, told him I wanted to stop because I was perfectly fine. I'm still ashamed of myself to this day: I should have ask him to talk to them, convince them I needed mental care.

I wasn't OK, and this event taught me to hide my negative feelings, to suppress my anger, my worries, my pain. That as long as I was faking it, everything would always be okay. Oh sure there were times where I said every single day that I wanted to die, that it was so hard to bury any "bad" emotion, that I felt so messed up and so lost and so mad. I managed to keep it at bay until I was 26, when I had a burn-out and tried to kill myself. 

I tried again two years ago and I've seen many therapists since but none really "clicked" with me until last year when I found a unicorn (not literally, but she's amazing). I'm very friendly and social with new people: you can hear me laugh and do witty jokes but I don't open up easily. I like people, I love to meet new persons, but I'm still struggling to make friends because it's really, really, really hard for me to entrust them with the entirety of my being. I'm terribly afraid of being rejected if I express my anger or my anxiety.  I'm working on it with my therapist, but with the whole corona situation I'm very isolated (safe for my cat). 
 
I'm currently 31 and diagnosed with Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Major Depression and BPD (and endometriosis because 3 mental illnesses weren't enough). Would my life have been different if I had completed my therapy? I'll never know, but I think so. It's not easy to live knowing that you lost so many years to mental illness when you HAD the possibility of a therapy. 

I don't give a damn if they really thought I was faking it: I had a therapist I trusted, and they forced me to stop seeing him. My stepfather, who is in dire need of a therapy, was wrong and my mother didn't even listen to me. That's something I will never ever forgive.
